about: A `required` field must have a value (LANGUAGE.md, Fields): every runtime's save refuses a record whose required field is empty, before anything is written and after the entity's `before save` event (which may fill it), so nothing is kept and a new record stays new. The refusal is Clarity's word `refusal.key` with its English `refusal.english`, its slot `{field}` the field's label in the person's language (a label written as a key takes the key's value; a plain one is shown as it is). It reaches code as any refusal does: the handler stops, and the window shows it as an error message. A case gives the entity's required fields in its order (`required`: each stored column and its label as written) and the values the record would store by column (`values`: JSON null is no value, a string text, a number a whole number, a bool a bool). `refused` is the label shown in the slot of the refusal, or null when the save goes on. Empty text and no value are empty; 0 and false are values.

cases.name: a reference to no record is refused
a date that is not set is refused
the first empty field in the entity's order is the one named
a field that is not required may stay empty
